# Gemba

> The agent-runtime platform. Stand up the environment, run agent sessions,
> read the traces, keep the memory, and measure the outcomes. Six commands and
> four CI actions run one loop.

Gemba is the platform a team hires to run coding agents continuously. In Lean
practice, gemba is the actual place where the work happens, and this platform
is where an agent team does the work. The loop is stand up, run, see, remember,
and measure. The platform ships that loop twice. It ships a command family for
a terminal and composite actions for GitHub Actions. What a team rehearses
locally is what runs on every push. Kata is the reference tenant. It runs this
platform every day, and it is a separate product with its own site at
https://www.kata.team/.

Six commands cover the loop. `gemba-harness` runs single-agent and multi-agent
sessions and captures one NDJSON trace. `gemba-trace` queries those traces for
turns, tool calls, errors, and token cost. `gemba-wiki` keeps persistent
memory as boot digests, claims, memos, and integrity audits. `gemba-xmr`
charts a metric as an XmR control chart, so the team acts on signal instead of
noise. `gemba-benchmark` grades a task family across repeated runs with hidden
tests and reports pass@k. `gemba-selfedit` gives a sandboxed agent a narrow,
audited path to edit its own instruction files.

Four published composite actions run the same loop in CI. `gemba-bootstrap`
installs the pinned toolchain and the platform CLIs. `gemba-harness` runs an
agent task and uploads the trace. `gemba-wiki` runs a memory command with a
freshly minted token. `gemba-benchmark` runs benchmark families across
machines and merges the reports. A workflow pins each action by SHA.

Install the skill pack with `apm install forwardimpact/gemba-skills`, then ask
Claude to stand up the team. For the commands alone, run
`npm install -g @forwardimpact/gemba`.
